boundaryBudgets.remediation: Replace explicit any with a narrow generic, unknown plus validation, or a modeled protocol type.
Remove the double assertion or validate the value before crossing the boundary.
Parse deserialized data through a named schema validator before treating it as a domain type.

allowlist.reason: Detector false positive: `decode(raw)` for a primitive value calls the decodeDelimited `decode: (value: string) => string` option (decodeComponent, decodeForm or identity), a string-to-string percent-decoder. Nothing is deserialized and no type is asserted; the value is coerced by the schema resolver next.

Detector false positive: `decode(item)` for an array item calls the decodeDelimited `decode: (value: string) => string` option (decodeComponent, decodeForm or identity), a string-to-string percent-decoder. Nothing is deserialized and no type is asserted; the value is coerced by the schema resolver next.

Detector false positive: `decode(rawKey)` for an object key calls the decodeDelimited `decode: (value: string) => string` option (decodeComponent, decodeForm or identity), a string-to-string percent-decoder. Nothing is deserialized and no type is asserted; the value is coerced by the schema resolver next.

Detector false positive: `decode(rawValue)` for an object value calls the decodeDelimited `decode: (value: string) => string` option (decodeComponent, decodeForm or identity), a string-to-string percent-decoder. Nothing is deserialized and no type is asserted; the value is coerced by the schema resolver next.

Detector false positive (syntactic): readBody is the generic media-type body codec and returns the JSON.parse result typed `unknown` (syntax errors become PARSE_ERROR). It asserts no domain type; every consumer checks the shape it relies on (decodeInput requires a non-array object for spread bodies, errorFromHttpResponse reads fields through typeof guards, RpcServer.call validates the assembled input against the procedure schema). A validator at this layer could only check 'is a JSON value', which JSON.parse already guarantees.

Detector false positive (syntactic): parseContent decodes a content-based (application/json) parameter and returns it typed `unknown` (syntax errors become BAD_REQUEST). No domain type is asserted; RpcServer.call validates the call input it is placed into against the procedure input schema.

Detector false positive: `textDecoder.decode(slice)` in readString is a TextDecoder turning the UTF-8 bytes of a MessagePack str (length bounds-checked by take(size)) into a plain JS string. No structured value is produced.

Detector false positive: `sharedTextDecoder.decode(raw)` turns L3 fetch bytes into a plain string; the next statement parses it with StoredChunkDescriptorSchema.parse(JSON.parse(text)), which the detector counts as validated.

Detector false positive: `decoder.decode(value, { stream: true })` is a streaming TextDecoder appending ReadableStream<Uint8Array> bytes to the NDJSON line buffer string. No structured value is produced at this call.

Detector false positive: `strictUtf8.decode(...)` is a fatal TextDecoder that turns an assembled WebSocket text message into a JS string and throws on invalid UTF-8 (the relay then closes with 1007). It produces a plain string, not structured data; every frame parsed from that string goes through PeerFrameSchema.parse(JSON.parse(text)) in peer-server.ts.
